title: Five recession samples reject selective flow removal that every equally spaced triple permits in one fixed-store test
abstract: We extend a three-sample selective flow removal test to full recession records of unchanged parallel linear stores. In one synthetic record, every equally spaced triple among five samples permits 80% retention of starting flow. All five samples together permit at most 78%. A nonnegative quartic polynomial proves this sharp bound, and positive atoms attain it. We also bound the smallest independent relative correction to all ten raw flows that restores model compatibility. Exact rational dual polynomials and a positive finite witness place this error between 0.0185403275% and 0.0185475681%. Thus added samples can reject a common store spectrum even when all triple tests pass, but a small flow error can remove that gain. The general matrix test uses established interval moment theory. An independent rational audit and 500 synthetic mixture checks are included. This is a method result, not a new Australian estimate. Comparable unforced events, nonnegative linear stores, selective removal and a specified error set limit field use. Code, proofs, certificates, source provenance and a figure support offline reproduction.

display.caption: All four equally spaced triples permit 80% retention, but the joint five-sample bound is 78%. Independent raw-flow corrections near 0.01855% remove that rejection in this synthetic test.
